messages:
maya: Quick heads-upworking on an interactive per-tenant SLO preview in the console. Goal: show estimated alert fanout, sample alerts, and a token/cost estimate while someone adjusts thresholds. Looking for API shape + perf constraints.

simon: Nice. Do you plan to run the sim client-side with sampled telemetry or hit a server endpoint?

maya: Server-side. We need access to historical telemetry, sampling configs, quiet windows, and routing rules. Proposed endpoint: POST /api/v1/slo/preview with body {tenant_id, slo_query, threshold, lookback_minutes, include_capacity=false, sampling_override?}.

ali: Warning a full fanout sim (resolving contacts, routes, escalation chains) per keystroke will spike CPU. Recommend two-path approach: 1) quick estimate using compact snapshot + precomputed aggregates for interactivity, 2) full-fidelity job enqueued for detailed breakdown.

nora: Snapshot approach makes sense. Maintain a read-optimized snapshot: tenant -> [route_map, contact_buckets, sampling_policy_id, snapshot_version]. Preview API must return snapshot_version so callers know if results are based on current policy.

maya: Agree. UI will show "based on snapshot v123 (60s stale)" and a "recompute now" button to force fresh sim. Also: anonymization required  don't surface email/phone numbers in preview. Show buckets like "pager on-call (2)" or "alerts to slack-channel #ops".

simon: How do we represent sampling in the response? Users need to understand how much sampling reduces notifications vs raw triggers.

maya: Response fields (stringified in the message): raw_triggers, sampled_triggers, sampling_strategy_id, top_buckets:[{bucket_label, sampled_count, escalation_level}], estimated_tokens_cost, confidence_pct, snapshot_version, quick (true|false). Quick = true indicates fast-path heuristics used.

ali: Implementation notes:  quick path should only consult snapshot + small in-memory heuristics. Full path resolves escalation trees but should not call downstream notify service for each sim; use the snapshot mapping instead. Also add per-tenant and per-user rate limits, e.g., 10 quick sims/min and 1 full sim/min per user.

nora: On routing & capacity: modeling real-time capacity is expensive. Default: resolve routing by policy order and ignore capacity. Add include_capacity=true to run a cheaper capacity heuristic (slot-based fallback) for full sims. Make this opt-in.

maya: Rollout flow idea: after preview, console offers "Save as experiment" to test new threshold across X% of tenants. API: POST /api/v1/slo/experiments {baseline, candidate, pct, duration, snapshot_version} -> returns {experiment_id, projected_global_impact}. Require snapshot_version to avoid surprise drift between preview and rollout.

simon: Good call on snapshot_version. Also require a re-sim if snapshot_version is older than N seconds during experiment creation (safety check).

ali: Telemetry: emit metrics with low cardinality: slo_preview.request{tenant_hash, quick=true/false, sampling_override?}, slo_preview.result{tenant_hash, quick, raw_triggers_bucket, sampled_triggers_bucket, confidence_bucket}. Also emit experiment.create events. Keep strings and buckets to keep metric volumes sane.

nora: Ops thread: sims may create queue pressure. Suggest a small preview worker pool and backpressure responses (HTTP 202 + poll_url) when queue length > threshold. UI can degrade gracefully showing "detailed estimate queued (ETA ~10s)".

maya: UX: show quick estimate immediately and a second card that updates when the detailed sim finishes. Also surface anonymized examples of alerts (no identifiers) to help users sanity-check routing and escalation.

simon: Rate-limiting + auth: previews should be scoped by RBAC. If user lacks contact read permissions, UI shows anonymized view only. Also log preview access for audit.

deploy-bot: reminder: infra deploy window tonight 02:00-03:00 UTC. If schema changes or new DB columns needed, schedule a migration plan.

maya: Action items: 1) ali to draft OpenAPI snippet + rate limits, 2) nora to propose snapshot schema and queue/backpressure policy, 3) maya to wire quick/full UX states and anonymization text, 4) sim-team to prototype cost_estimate heuristics. I'll pull into a short RFC after initial sketches.

ali: I'll post an OpenAPI draft and rate-limit numbers in this thread by EOD.

nora: I'll prototype a snapshot JSON example and a tiny cost function (tokens->$).

maya: Thanks all  will follow up with RFC. :thumbsup:
